scope: Exact full 4105-target end-to-end commitProof allocation boundary, authorized by msg_adee7129aa6b
not_acceptance: Allocation characterization only. Not a latency measurement, not a speed claim, not production acceptance. ns/op is recorded for ordering only and is not a result: 5 iterations on a shared host.

inside: buildStateProof(st, fp, nilPrior, withPrior, hashes, detected)

attribution.residual_meaning: 0.006% of bytes. The components are separately measured calls that sum to the separately measured whole, so this is measured attribution, not summed phase marks.

correction_to_prior_incomplete_figure.prior_was: 50.16% of actual bytes, 99.41% of actual allocations

correction_to_prior_incomplete_figure.effect_of_the_19_HTML_targets_and_real_i: build+stage at the real 4105-target inventory is 1365242 B/op and 28922 allocs/op, within 0.08% of bytes and 0.11% of allocations of the 4086-owner fixture. The understatement was the omitted selections, not the missing targets. This replaces the unmeasured extrapolation withdrawn in msg_69e7858b7a95 with a measurement.

reference_comparison.same_pass: CommitProofWhole 2719507 B/op 29062 allocs/op; StateMarshalProductSize 129557440 B/op 652841 allocs/op; StateWriteProductSize 129562747 B/op 652866 allocs/op
reference_comparison.instability_disclosed: State marshal bytes/op is not stable across iteration counts: 171514784 B/op at -benchtime=3x versus 129557440 B/op at 5x, while allocs/op moved only 652859 to 652841. Encoder buffer growth amortizes differently, so the bytes ratio is a range of roughly 1.6% to 2.1% rather than one number. Allocation ratio is stable at about 4.45%.
reference_comparison.reading: commitProof is an allocation-count cost concentrated in buildStateProof, plus a byte cost that is half selection slices and half proof build, to produce 10966 output bytes.

limitations: Bytes and allocations only. No latency acceptance, no comparison against the Stage20 baseline, no claim about the measured body or structural regressions.
Shared host, 5 iterations per benchmark, no repeat series.
The state is a fixed decoded snapshot reused across iterations; a real commit builds it in the same run, so state construction cost is outside this boundary by design.
filesToHash reads inventory and policy only, so both selections are pure recomputation here; in a real run they follow a fresh Inventory whose cost is outside this boundary.
Promotion is measured with the stage re-done outside the timer each iteration, because promotePendingProof consumes the staged file.
Root's own in-run marks (proof written 31ms, build 19.8ms nested, promote 5ms on o4-body) remain the authoritative timing evidence; nothing here supersedes them.
